subject: Acme renewal + expansion recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme renewal + expansion recap & next steps

Hi Jenna — great to chat this morning. Thanks for taking the time to walk through Acme's usage and the Q3 roadmap. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key points, confirm the pain areas, and outline proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of the call
- Current relationship: hosted API usage (text gen + embeddings) with peak latency issues during morning batch jobs and some token-cost surprises in April.
- Usage: ~1.2B tokens/month avg, embeddings ~120k/month; growth trend ~15% month-over-month (see attached Acme_USAGE_Q1_Q2.csv).
- Primary goals: 1) stabilize latency for customer-facing features, 2) reduce per-token costs for batch workloads, 3) pilot semantic search for support tickets by end of Q3.
- Pain points: latency spikes at peak hours (~800–1,200ms p95), occasional model quality regressions after model swaps, and lack of clear cost predictability for monthly forecasting.

Recommended path (high level)
- Renewal + Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool to guarantee throughput and lower p95 latency.
- Pilot workloads: run support-ticket summarization on a Dedicated pool with a small reserved commit for 6–8 weeks to validate latency and cost.
- Redwood Optimize: enable batching/caching presets and quantization recommendations for your summarization pipeline to reduce token cost.

Proposed timeline
- Week 1 (this week): exchange procurement contact and legal point-of-contact; I’ll share a draft mutual action plan and SOW.
- Week 2–3: pricing & commercial review with Rishi; finalize committed capacity options.
- 6–8 weeks after sign: pilot kickoff for support-ticket summarization (tech kickoff suggested week of June 8).

Open asks/next steps for Acme
- Confirm procurement/legal contact (procurement@acme.com is fine if correct).
- Confirm the three pilot workloads and expected QPS for ticket summarization.
- Any additional compliance docs needed (SOC2 evidence, data flow diagrams)? We can surface those quickly.

Attachments: Acme_USAGE_Q1_Q2.csv (usage export), Mutual_Action_Plan_Acme.pdf (draft MAP)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the mutual action plan and a draft SOW by next Tuesday.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick notes:

- Procurement contact is procurement@acme.com (cc’d our procurement alias here). Please also loop in our legal reviewer, John Lee (john.lee@acme.com) on the SOW.
- Confirming the pilot workload: ticket summarization (~300 TPS during peak digest jobs) and embeddings-based search for our internal KB. We’d like the pilot to start mid-June if possible.
- For compliance, SOC2 Type II report and a brief data retention policy would be great.

Can you include a rough pricing ballpark for the Dedicated reserved option in the SOW/draft? That will help prep internally.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the MAP.

Jenna

Looping in pricing notes for the thread — quick internal sync:

- Pricing sketch for conversation: 12-month committed Dedicated pool sized for current peak + 25% buffer. Ballpark: $95k/month list, with an introductory commit discount of 18% for the first 12 months + one month of migration assistance included.
- Upsell path: once pilot validates latency/cost, propose adding a second Dedicated pool optimized for batch (quantized models) at an incremental $25k/month (after discount).
- I’ll draft a short pricing appendix to include in the SOW and add a HubSpot deal note (see link).

Marissa/Rachel — if you want, I can draft the pricing appendix and share as a Google doc by end of day.
